column1: # The state folder rule (docs/CONVERSATION_CACHE.md "Where the state folder can be"): one table, two implementations.
# tests/state_root_test.cpp runs it against engine/runtime/state_root.h, tests/test_state_root_rule.py against
# tools/crucible_cli/state_root.py state_root_verdict. Both must give the code in the last column.
# Columns (tab separated): name, setup, path, uid, gid, code.
# setup: steps joined by ';' (or '-' for none): `dir P MODE` makes a folder and sets its octal mode, `file P` makes a file,
#   `link P TARGET` makes a symbolic link. In setup and path, T is a fresh folder of this case (mode 0700) and H is the
#   home folder T/home (mode 0700). S is a fresh folder directly inside /tmp (a root folder with the sticky bit); a row
#   that names S is skipped when /tmp is not such a folder. ID is an identity folder name (3 groups of 16 hex digits).
# uid: self (this user) or other (a user that owns nothing here). gid: self (the group of T) or other.
# code: ok, or the refusal: relative, system, home, link, not-dir, parent-owner, parent-open, owner, shared, foreign,
#   unreadable (the path cannot be read: a path fault), contents-unreadable (the list of the folder cannot be read).
